title: SLEEP: periodic consolidation for continual learning

claims.text: Google Research’s October 27, 2026 post describes alternating active interaction with offline consolidation. The sleep phase updates numerical weights within a fixed architecture and predefined training rules.
Consolidation combines additional low-rank memory experts with distillation. A separate dreaming stage varies expert activation, selects synthetic practice data and refines the model.
The authors report long-context results reaching 10 million tokens on BABILong and sequential-learning results intended to reduce forgetting. These are experiment-specific publisher claims.

limitations: Results were not independently reproduced here.
This is a model-training proposal; its benefits cannot be assumed for an ordinary file-search archive.
gaps: The paper is archived separately; detailed experimental review remains pending.
The video’s visual explanations were not reviewed.
